title: Use of FIBxTEM to Investigate the Carbon Nanotube to Substrate Interaction of Direct and Indirect CNT Growth by Catalytic Chemical Vapor Deposition
content: Catalytic chemical vapor deposition (CCVD) is a flexible method for producing carbon nanotubes (CNTs) with a variety of properties. The most common method for CCVD growth of CNTs involves an indirect substrate, such as silicon, in which a catalyst layer (usually iron oxide) is deposited on the surface. A diffusion barrier layer, such as alumina, is also used to separate the catalyst from the substrate and prevent the formation of intermetallics [1]. By heating the substrate in a reductive atmosphere, such as hydrogen, the iron oxides are reduced into catalyst nanoparticles on the surface of the substrate. A hydrocarbon gas is then flowed over the catalysts at high temperatures causing thermal decomposition of the precursor. Excess carbon is then absorbed and extruded from the catalyst as a CNT [2].
